claim: FIFO storage is the largest functional consumer of the committed unconstrained trng_digital netlist (10,542.6 um2 of 22,203.8, 47.5%, conclusive against the shared/unassigned residual); a depth-2 FIFO variant synthesizes at 16,129.2 um2 (-27.4% vs same-tool baseline) and, while it diverges from the depth-4 normative model at the depth-observable checks, it MATCHES the normative model's own fifo_depth=2 parameterisation bit-for-bit over the full 4239-cycle directed program (RTL and mapped netlist); a folded sampler_core (F1) estimates 218.675 x 81.94 um with ring symmetry intact; composition overhead is 37.08% of the committed whole block and 75% of it sits in the two stacking-artifact rectangles (an occupancy share, not a recovered area: across the study's own same-macro fixed-pin-edge vs edge-aligned estimates the recovery is -659 to +10,715 um2, positive only when the analog row is no wider than the digital macro; geometric estimate); no fixed-pin-edge combination reaches 0.05 mm2 -- best fixed-pin-edge estimate 0.060740 mm2 (1.215x), best edge-aligned geometric estimate 0.055898 mm2 (needs a pin-access check); the routed digital macro remains the largest limiter
author: loom-builder@sky130-trng

fold_f1.description: six samplers folded into two rows of three; ro_array_core ring row geometry unchanged (all four rings in one committed row, 55.3 um pitch)

routing.model: per-net Manhattan length between the folded endpoints (committed port coordinates; sampler row B moved to the row-A x origins one row offset up, array one more row offset up) plus the committed polyline's own detour excess
assumed_detours: ro1 descends the west margin lane (x = -2.0) instead of the committed x = -0.5 column, +3.0 um
the supply straps re-tap row B's rails at their east end (x = 161.79); a vss/vdd rail extension beyond the row end is assumed legal -- no DRC was run
routing.not_modelled: via counts, layer-change delays, track congestion in the new row-A/row-B gap, and timing/coupling effects of the shorter or longer data hauls

fold_f1.symmetry_verdict: survives by construction: the four rings keep their committed single-row arrangement, pitch and per-ring vddr1..vddr4 rails byte-for-byte
fold_f1.supply_verdict: vddr1..vddr4 per-ring rails unchanged; the shared vdd/vss straps and the clk/rst_n lanes need one extra horizontal run per folded row plus two vertical risers each (met1/met2, same style as the committed strap stages)
fold_f1.added_routing_estimate: see routing (recomputed from the folded endpoints)

fold_f2.description: samplers 3+3 AND the four rings in a 2x2 grid (equal 55.3 um pitch both axes); buffers and xor tree beside the grid
fold_f2.symmetry_verdict: does NOT survive verbatim: every ring gains a vertical neighbour no committed record measures; DR-0003 section 8's decorrelation caveat applies to the new adjacency
fold_f2.supply_verdict: vddr rails per ring unchanged, but the rail routing and the well/strap pattern between grid rows are new geometry
fold_f2.added_routing_estimate: strap/lane doubling as F1 plus re-plumbed ring-to-xor routes; not derived further -- recorded as the wider/lower-confidence alternative

item2_fold.basis: placement dry run: bbox arithmetic over the committed compose geometry (cell.json origins, compose.response.json bboxes); no GDS composed, no DRC/LVS run

item3_composition_overhead.basis: axis-aligned decomposition of the committed whole-block bbox (layout/trng_whole/report.json), cut on the committed macro bboxes; measured inputs, exact rectangle arithmetic

removable_by_tighter_floorplan.interpretation: occupancy share of the overhead sitting in the two named stacking-artifact rectangles; NOT a recovered area -- recovery depends on the before/after floorplan (see item4_combine fixed-vs-edge-aligned rows)
removable_by_tighter_floorplan.condition: the analog row's width and west edge are matched to the digital macro's footprint in a re-stack (folded analog narrower than the digital macro, or an explicit re-stack that aligns west edges)

functional_overhead.note: lanes, boundary pads and the supply escape are contractual composition structure; they scale with width/height rather than vanish

item4_combine.best_option: variant FIFO-2 digital (die est) + folded analog F1
item4_combine.best_edge_aligned_option: variant FIFO-2 digital (die est) + folded analog F2 (2x2 rings), edge-aligned
item4_combine.verdict_text: Within the fixed pin-edge topology (digital east pin edge held, as committed) no studied combination reaches 0.05 mm2: the best is 0.060740 mm2 (1.215x target), short by 0.010740 mm2. The best edge-aligned geometric estimate -- a floorplan change that also needs a pin-access check -- is 0.055898 mm2 (variant FIFO-2 digital (die est) + folded analog F2 (2x2 rings), edge-aligned); it does not reach the target. Trade-off, not a requirement: holding the F1 analog width (218.675 um) and dimensions, the digital macro would have to be at most 116.6 um tall (a hypothetical re-stack at that size is 0.050000 mm2) vs the 165.7 um the FIFO-2 variant estimates -- about 49% of its die area; narrowing the analog row or aligning edges relaxes that digital budget.
item4_combine.largest_remaining_limiter: the routed digital macro: even with the FIFO-2 variant its estimated die is ~27449 um2 at the achieved 62% utilisation of #251's repaired 65% point -- the largest single contributor of the best row; the analog F1 bbox (17918 um2) is second, the functional composition overhead (lane band + pads + escape, scaling with width) third
